title: Salmonella, E. coli, norovirus are some of the common foodborne germs - WCVB

analysis.time: Published 2026-07-17 16:04 EDT; event period covers 2026 multistate cyclosporiasis outbreak and general guidance on foodborne pathogens.
analysis.location_and_population: United States (Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, West Virginia) with implicated produce sourced from Mexico; general U.S. population guidance.
analysis.event: CDC issued a multistate outbreak notice linking Cyclospora infections to iceberg lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms to Taco Bell; guidance article explains Cyclospora transmission, symptoms, and prevention.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: More than 1,600 illnesses reported in the Taco Bell-associated outbreak; nationally, about 48 million foodborne illnesses, 128,000 hospitalizations, and 3,000 deaths occur annually in the U.S.; Salmonella causes the most outbreak notices (116 since 2006), the most deaths, and about 1.35 million infections per year; norovirus is the leading cause of foodborne illness and hospitalizations.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: CDC and FDA investigating the Taco Bell-linked outbreak; supplier traced to a single iceberg lettuce source from Mexico; Taco Bell is removing implicated lettuce; CDC continues to investigate other unrelated cyclosporiasis outbreaks; guidance emphasizes washing produce with clean water and manual cleaning due to rough surfaces; no evidence of person-to-person transmission; antibiotic therapy reserved for severe or persistent cases.

analysis.brief_en: On July 17, 2026, U.S. health authorities linked a multistate outbreak of cyclosporiasis to iceberg lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms to Taco Bell, with more than 1,600 illnesses reported across Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and West Virginia. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued its eighth multistate foodborne-outbreak notice of the year, underscoring heightened public-health concern. Cyclospora, a foodborne parasite, causes explosive watery diarrhea and typically resolves without treatment, though antibiotics are needed in severe cases. The outbreak highlights the challenge of removing Cyclospora from produce with rough surfaces like lettuce, cilantro, and berries. Authorities recommend vigorous washing and manual cleaning; person-to-person spread has not been documented. Separately, CDC data show Salmonella remains the leading cause of foodborne deaths and outbreak notices, while norovirus causes the most illnesses and hospitalizations annually.

title: Princess Cruises ship docks at Port Canaveral after norovirus outbreak - AOL.com

analysis.time: Event date: April 28–May 11, 2026; Publication date: May 11, 2026 (docking day); Reported illness onsets by May 7, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: United States (Florida): Port Canaveral (Cruise Terminal 6) and Port Everglades (Fort Lauderdale); cruise itinerary included Nassau, Bahamas.
analysis.event: A norovirus outbreak occurred aboard the Princess Cruises ship Caribbean Princess during a nearly two-week voyage; the ship docked at Port Canaveral on May 11, 2026, after Bahamian port officials declined clearance to dock in Nassau due to public-health concerns.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 102 of 3,116 passengers (3.3%) and 13 of 1,131 crew members (1.1%) reported gastrointestinal illness consistent with norovirus; predominant symptoms were diarrhea and vomiting; no deaths reported; outbreak response included isolation, enhanced cleaning, and specimen collection.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: CDC guidance followed; crew isolated ill passengers and crew, increased cleaning and disinfection, and collected stool specimens; ship underwent comprehensive cleaning before next departure; passengers compensated for missed Nassau port; Princess Cruises stated health and community safety were prioritized; uncertainty remains regarding exact transmission source and full extent of secondary spread.

analysis.brief_en: The Caribbean Princess cruise ship returned to Port Canaveral, Florida, on May 11, 2026, after a norovirus outbreak sickened 115 people—102 passengers and 13 crew—during a two-week voyage that began April 28. The outbreak prompted enhanced sanitation measures, isolation of ill individuals, and specimen collection, in line with U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention protocols. Bahamian authorities denied docking in Nassau out of caution ahead of local elections, leading to itinerary changes and passenger compensation. Princess Cruises emphasized adherence to global health guidelines and coordination with authorities to protect guests and destinations. No deaths were reported, and the ship prepared for comprehensive disinfection before its next departure.

analysis.time: Published on 2026-07-17; event occurred during voyage dates June 12–July 2, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: San Francisco (departure/return port), Alaska and Canada round-trip voyage; affected population: 3,032 guests and crew aboard Ruby Princess cruise ship.
analysis.event: Reported norovirus outbreak aboard Princess Cruises’ Ruby Princess, confirmed by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); Princess Cruises acknowledged cases and implemented control measures.

Experts note that while norovirus is common, cruise-ship clusters represent only about 1% of all U.S. outbreaks.

analysis.location_and_population: Alaska, USA; National Geographic Sea Bird expedition cruise ship operated by Lindblad Expeditions; affected passengers and crew.

title: 145 People Sickened In Norovirus Outbreaks On Cruise Ships: What To Know - AOL.com

analysis.time: Published 2026-07-16; event dates: Ruby Princess voyage 2026-06-12 to 2026-07-02, National Geographic Sea Bird voyages 2026-05-25–2026-05-30 and 2026-06-25 to 2026-06-30; reports to CDC Vessel Sanitation Program on 2026-06-28.
analysis.location_and_population: Pacific Ocean and Alaskan coastal waters; Ruby Princess (Princess Cruises) and National Geographic Sea Bird (Lindblad Expeditions); passengers and crew aboard these ships.
analysis.event: Reported norovirus outbreaks on two cruise ships confirmed by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); investigation ongoing.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 145 cases: Ruby Princess 125 (102 passengers, 23 crew), National Geographic Sea Bird 20 (19 passengers, 1 crew); symptoms included vomiting and diarrhea; no deaths reported; risk of continued gastrointestinal illness outbreaks on cruise ships.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: CDC Vessel Sanitation Program notified on 2026-06-28; ships increased cleaning, isolated sick individuals, and consulted CDC; stool samples collected on Ruby Princess; second Sea Bird outbreak within a month; cause of May Sea Bird outbreak unknown; seven cruise outbreak reports received by CDC in 2026 to date.

analysis.brief_en: Federal health officials confirmed norovirus outbreaks sickening 145 people across two cruise ships—the Ruby Princess and the National Geographic Sea Bird—operating in the Pacific and Alaskan waters. On the Ruby Princess, 102 of 3,032 passengers and 23 of 1,144 crew fell ill during a voyage from San Francisco to Alaska between June 12 and July 2. The Sea Bird reported 19 of 68 passengers and one crew member sick during a June 25–30 trip, marking its second gastrointestinal outbreak in about a month; the earlier late-May outbreak’s cause remains unknown. Both ships notified the CDC’s Vessel Sanitation Program on June 28. Princess Cruises collected stool samples for testing, while both operators intensified cleaning, isolated affected individuals, and coordinated with the CDC. No deaths have been reported, but the incidents underscore ongoing risks of norovirus transmission on cruise vessels.

Both ships notified the CDC’s Vessel Sanitation Program on June 28. No deaths have been reported, but the incidents underscore ongoing risks of norovirus transmission on cruise vessels.

title: Alaska cruise struck by third suspected norovirus outbreak in weeks - The News International

analysis.time: Published 17 July 2026; event occurred 10–15 July 2026 aboard a cruise between those dates.
analysis.location_and_population: Alaska waters aboard Lindblad Expeditions' National Geographic Sea Bird; affected population: 18 of 62 passengers.
analysis.event: Third suspected norovirus outbreak reported on the cruise ship; cause currently listed as unknown by CDC; previous two outbreaks in May and June were confirmed norovirus.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 18 cases of gastrointestinal illness (vomiting and abdominal cramps) among 62 passengers; no deaths reported; risk of further spread via contaminated food, water, surfaces, or close contact.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: CDC remotely monitoring situation; cruise operator isolated sick passengers and crew, collected stool samples for testing, consulted CDC Vessel Sanitation Program, and increased cleaning and disinfection; cause confirmation pending; CDC notes norovirus is a common cause of cruise ship outbreaks but source confirmation can take time.

analysis.brief_en: A cruise ship operating in Alaska waters has reported its third gastrointestinal illness outbreak in two months, with 18 of 62 passengers falling ill between 10 and 15 July 2026. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has not yet confirmed the cause, although the ship’s previous two outbreaks in May and June were confirmed as norovirus. The agency is remotely monitoring the situation while the operator has isolated affected individuals, collected samples for testing, and intensified sanitation measures. Norovirus spreads easily via contaminated food, water, surfaces, or close contact, and while the current risk remains localized to the vessel, the repeated outbreaks raise concerns about onboard hygiene practices.

The agency is remotely monitoring the situation while the operator has isolated affected individuals, collected samples for testing, and intensified sanitation measures. Norovirus spreads easily via contaminated food, water, surfaces, or close contact, and while the current risk remains localized to the vessel, the repeated outbreaks raise concerns about onboard hygiene practices.
